author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Frances Tiafoe reached the U.S. Open semifinals for the third time after rallying from two sets and a break down against fellow American Alex Michelsen.
The 11th seed won 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6(6) on Tuesday at Arthur Ashe Stadium, Reuters reported. Michelsen served for the match in the third set, but Tiafoe broke back and shifted the momentum.
The victory set up an all-American semifinal against Ben Shelton, who later defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz. It guarantees a U.S. player a place in the men’s final.

Tiafoe also reached the tournament’s semifinals in 2022 and 2024. His latest run keeps alive the effort to end a long drought in American men’s major singles tennis: Andy Roddick remains the last U.S. man to win a Grand Slam title, at the 2003 U.S. Open. The semifinal matchup is now fixed, but its schedule and any later tournament details should be confirmed with organizers.
dek: The American recovered from two sets and a break down to beat Alex Michelsen and earn a semifinal meeting with Ben Shelton.
headline: Frances Tiafoe completes comeback to reach U.S. Open semifinals
